title: lampOS control protocol, v1
description: Every frame on wss://<lamp>.local:7731/v1, one JSON object per text frame: a request from the client, a reply or an event from the lamp. docs/control.md says what each means; this file is what the SDKs generate from. Not served yet: lamp-control is a design (#3504).

id.description: The client's number for a request, echoed as `re` in its reply.

time.description: A time in UTC, RFC 3339 with `Z` (`2026-10-27T08:40:01Z`), as lamp-control writes it; a client turns it into local time itself.

grant.description: What a paired client may do. body: gestures, moves, look, joints; light; speak: say and sound; look: presence events; hear: registered phrases; sound: sound classes; skills: its own skills put on the lamp, which run on their own after it goes; air: the air sensor's readings (get air, air.changed); device: the lamp's own processor, memory, disk and temperatures (get device); camera: the camera's pictures (camera.snapshot, camera.stream), never while the lamp is private; microphone: the microphone's sound (microphone.stream), never while the lamp is private; speaker: sound played through the lamp's speaker, any sound and not only the lamp's own voice (speaker.stream), never while the lamp is private; notes: its own small key/value notes kept on the lamp (notes.set, notes.get, notes.delete, notes.list), gone with its revoke; speech: every line the lamp says out loud (lamp.said), which can be personal, never what a person says to it.

part.description: What a lease holds: voice is say and sound.

pattern.description: lamp_msgs::PatternKind: a breath, a candle's wander, one soft pulse around. Never a blink or a flash.

gesture.description: A body clip (crates/body/src/clips/data.rs) by name. The door checks only the name's shape, as lamp-control's plain_name (a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, at most 64), and the body answers a name it doesn't have. `examples` are the clips offered to programs (skills and add-ons name these); `idle`, the lamp's own life, and `scanning`, a room sweep, are taken too.

joint.description: A joint's target in degrees from its pose.

frame.description: One step of a move: head pitch, head roll, base yaw, shoulder, elbow, in counts from the pose (4,096 a turn), as moves/*.json. At most 1,300 either way here (the ceiling any lamp could take); the body holds each joint to its own reach.

pair.description: Once per computer, with the one-time code the owner's app shows (or the lamp says after a 3 s hold of its button).

name.description: The computer's name, shown in the app.

key.description: The client's Ed25519 public key, base64 (32 bytes).

proof.description: HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the code's 8 ASCII digits, over "lampos/v1/pair" and a zero byte, the pin's 32 bytes (the certificate's full SHA-256, from the owner's app), the 32 key bytes, then the welcome's 32 nonce bytes; base64.

hello.description: First on every connection of a paired client.

sig.description: The client key's Ed25519 signature over "lampos/v1/hello" and a zero byte, then the welcome's 32 nonce bytes; base64 (64 bytes).

token.description: On the control socket only (/run/lampos-control/control.sock): the one-run token a skill's run holds, 43 characters of base64url; the client is then c_0 and the sig 64 zero bytes. A secret: never logged.

phrases.description: For phrase.heard: matched on the lamp; the client is told only which matched, never what was said.

items.description: 8 letters at least, so no short word or pair.

allOf.description: phrase.heard needs the phrases to listen for.

for_ms.description: At most 10 min a take or renewal; renewed in time, a lease is held as long as its holder renews.

why.description: Journaled and shown in the app.

express.description: A feeling in body and light, as the lamp shows its own (the feelings skill, #3691): its move and its light. Its names are that skill's, glad, lively and low today; any other is bad_request. strength from 0.5 up plays the skill's whole move, below it a three-quarter, half or quarter step of it, never bigger.

oneOf.description: At the face it sees (needs look); at the hand it sees, followed by the body until stop, another look or the lease ends (needs look); the person who called its name; or straight ahead.
Degrees from straight ahead: yaw right positive, pitch up positive; any finite number, the body clamps it to its gaze reach (the done says `clamped`).

look.description: Needs a body lease held by this client.

move.description: A move of the client's own, needs a body lease held by this client. Its first and last frames are all 0; the body's move check (moves.rs) judges the rest: 1.5 to 10 s, each joint's farthest and fastest. The last frame is all 0 too, which the crate checks; the schema can say only the first.

step_ms.description: The body's own: 40 to 1000, and the move lasts 1.5 to 10 s ((frames - 1) x step_ms), each joint within the body's reach and speed (lamp_body::moves::check); a move the body would drop is refused at the door.

frames.description: At least 2; at most what the body's move check allows (10 s at the shortest step, 40 ms: 251 frames).

prefixItems.description: The first frame is the pose: all 0.

play.description: A recorded move of one of this computer's pushed skills (its moves/NAME.json, kept when skill.push installed the skill), sent as a move of the same frames is; needs a body lease held by this client. skill says which when two of its skills have the name; the lamp refuses an ambiguous name, naming them.

skill.description: The pushed skill whose moves/ has the move, when two have the name.

joints.description: Joint targets, at most 40 a second, each step through the body's caps.

light.description: A light for a while, below the person and the conversation: one of the ring's named colours at a level (with an optional pattern), or the computer's own colour (rgb) or each pixel's (pixels, as many as hello's limits.ring.pixels), at a brightness. Exactly one of colour, rgb or pixels.

rgb.description: One colour for the whole ring, #rrggbb.

pixels.description: Each pixel's colour, #rrggbb, from pixel 0 around the ring: exactly hello's limits.ring.pixels of them.

brightness.description: With rgb or pixels: 0 to 100 of the given colours, under the ring's own channel ceiling (lower at night). 100 when not given.

fade_ms.description: How slowly the ring comes into this light.

say.description: A line in the lamp's own voice: spoken exactly as sent, straight through the speech service with no model, once the person isn't talking; with rephrase, said by the voice's model in its own words, as before. Through the privacy switch, the keeper's pause, and its quiet hours when set.

text.description: Words, at most 900 UTF-8 bytes, the voice's own cap (lamp-voice's MOST_WORDS_BYTES; hello's limits say_max_bytes). JSON Schema can't count bytes, so lamp-control checks it.

rephrase.description: true: the voice's model says it in its own words (a written turn), as before. Default false: exactly as sent.

sound.description: A sound, by name: `hum`, the voice's built-in short hum, through the voice's quiet, rarity and privacy gates; or one of this computer's own clips (sound.upload), played as an exact say is, once the person isn't talking, refused paused, muted or in quiet hours, with no rarity. Its `done` follows, as a say's does.

sound_name.description: `hum`, the lamp's own, or a clip's name: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, at most 64.

sound.upload.description: One part of a clip of this computer's own, sent in order from part 0: a WAV of 16-bit mono PCM at 24 kHz, at most 30 s, no sample past -12 dBFS and no 10 ms past -30 dBFS RMS (the voice's own bound). Each part's answer carries got; the last part's carries sound, once the clip is checked and kept, over one of the same name. A computer keeps at most 64 clips and 20 MB (hello's limits.sounds); a revoke deletes them.

sound.list.description: This computer's own clips: the reply's sounds.

sound.remove.description: One of this computer's own clips, deleted: the reply's removed.

notes_key.description: A note's key: 1 to 64 bytes of letters, digits and . _ : -.

notes.set.description: Keeps a note of this computer's own under a key, over one of the same key: the reply's key and bytes (the value serialized). The value is any JSON, at most 16384 bytes serialized; a computer keeps at most 256 keys and 262144 bytes of keys and values in all (hello's limits.notes). Needs the notes grant.

notes.get.description: One of this computer's own notes: the reply's key, found and, when found, value. A key not kept is found false, not an error.

notes.delete.description: One of this computer's own notes dropped: the reply's key and deleted (false when it was not kept).

notes.list.description: This computer's own keys that start with prefix (all when it is left out), sorted: the reply's keys (each key and the bytes of its value), count (those listed), total (all it keeps), bytes (all its keys and values take), keys_max and bytes_max.

clip.description: A clip of this computer's own, as sound.upload and sound.list say it.

stop.description: Ends the client's own actions now. Needs no grant and no lease.

turn.start.description: Opens a conversation turn as a tap on the head does: the person's next line is answered as spoken to the lamp. With `prompt`, the lamp says it first, as a say's words. Held to say's quiet hours and rate; needs speak and hear, and no lease. Answered `to: voice`; its `done` follows: finished once the turn's answer has sounded, else dropped with the voice's why.

prompt.description: Words, as say's text: at most 900 UTF-8 bytes, the voice's own cap (hello's limits say_max_bytes), no control characters. JSON Schema can't count bytes, so lamp-control checks it.

turn.end.description: Ends the turn this computer started, and the conversation grown from it; never another's. Needs speak. Answered `turn: ended` with `started`, the turn.start it ended; with no turn of this computer's, busy.

listen.set.description: This computer's mute: false holds it (`mute: held`) until it says true (`mute: lifted`, or `nothing_held`), its last connection closes, it is revoked, or a hand on the head lifts it, said as a done cut_short on the listen.set that held it. A stop doesn't lift it. Needs hear.

skill.push.description: One part of a skill package (lamp-skills pack's shape: ustar, lamp-skill.json first, then NAME/path), sent in order from 0; the last part's answer comes once the lamp has checked and installed it. Needs the skills grant.

name.description: A skill's name: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -.

data.description: This part's bytes, base64 (36 KiB of the package at most).

skill.list.description: This client's own pushed skills. Needs the skills grant.

skill.remove.description: One of this client's own pushed skills, taken off. Needs the skills grant.

name.description: A skill's name: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -.

oneOf.description: Taken. A pair reply carries client and grants; hello carries lamp, grants and limits; lease.take and lease.renew carry lease and until; get carries state, the states asked for by name; skill.push carries got for each part but the last, and skill (and moves) for the last; skill.list carries skills; camera.snapshot carries jpeg, bytes and age_ms; camera.stream carries stream and, on, fps and fps_now; sound.upload carries got for each part but the last, and sound for the last; sound.list carries sounds; sound.remove carries removed; notes.set carries key and bytes; notes.get carries key, found and, when found, value; notes.delete carries key and deleted; notes.list carries keys, count, total, bytes, keys_max and bytes_max; turn.end carries turn and started; listen.set carries mute; microphone.stream carries stream and, on, sample_rate, channels, format, block_ms and source.

re.description: The request's id, or null when it couldn't be read.

language.description: The owner's language (en, vi, ja, zh or ko), from the lamp's setup, so a program's own lines can follow it; en when the owner has not chosen one. Lamps from before this say none: read it as en.

state.description: get's answer: each state asked for, by its name. lamp-control's own: light and mood are null until known.

light.description: The person's own light (`on`, `colour`, `level`, from light/state), and `shows`: what the ring draws now (light/drawn), the person's light or one asked for over it. Each is left out until the lamp has said it; null until either is known. `shows.pixels` is optional (see its description).

pixels.description: Optional. The ring's own pixels, as a paired computer asked for them (`light` with `rgb` or `pixels`): present only while that computer holds them and the ring draws that light; left out otherwise, and on a lamp that does not say it. Each is `#rrggbb`, the colour asked of the ring (the ring's own channel ceiling may draw it dimmer).

air.description: get's air (the air grant): the newest reading with known: true, or only known: false.

pm1_0.description: Particles under 1 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm2_5.description: Particles under 2.5 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm4_0.description: Particles under 4 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm10.description: Particles under 10 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

humidity.description: Relative humidity at the sensor, percent, to a tenth.

temperature.description: Degrees Celsius at the sensor, to a tenth: inside the lamp's base, warmed by the lamp, so not the room's.

feel.description: How the air would feel, from the carbon dioxide: fresh under 800 ppm, fine to 1,200, stuffy to 2,000, very_stuffy past it, unknown without a reading.

known.description: Whether there is a reading: false with no sensor, its part not running, or none in 15 s, and then nothing else.

device.description: get's device (the device grant): the newest numbers with known: true, or only known: false.

cpu_load.description: The last minute's load over the processors: 1 is every processor busy.

memory_used.description: The share of memory in use.

disk_free.description: The share of the system disk free.

temperature_c.description: Each temperature the board reports, by its sensor's name, in degrees Celsius.

known.description: Whether there is a reading: false with no sensor, its part not running, or none in 15 s, and then nothing else.

volume.description: get's volume (the speak grant): the level speaker/volume last said, as volume.changed tells it; null until lamp-actions has said it.

level.description: 0 to 100 of what the lamp allows.

moves.description: With the last skill.push part's skill, on a lamp that has play: the moves of the package's moves/ that were kept for play, and the ones left out with why (the skill is installed either way).

age_ms.description: How old the picture was when read.

fps_now.description: camera.stream: the rate new frames came at lately, a second; null before any was measured.

fast.description: camera.stream: true when its frames come binary, every frame the camera makes.

result.description: service.read and service.write (a skill's run only): lamp-services' answer as it gave it, quoted data from the person's service or a write's read_back, held: true and next (never a send_id). Personal: never logged.

started.description: turn.end's: the id of the turn.start it ended.

channels.description: microphone.stream: channels interleaved in a block, 1.

format.description: microphone.stream: how a sample is written: s16le, signed 16 bits, low byte first.

block_ms.description: microphone.stream: how long one block is, 20 ms.

source.description: microphone.stream: which of the lamp's microphones: mic1, the room microphone the ears read.

re.description: The request's id, or null when it couldn't be read.

retry_ms.description: With rate: when the oldest counted action leaves its window.

error.description: A refusal. New fields may come; a client ignores what it doesn't know.

limits.description: hello's limits, as lamp-control's session::limits() says them: each rate class's windows (at most `most` in any `within_ms`), a light's and a lease's longest hold, the longest say, this lamp's quiet hours, and a computer's clips (sounds).

rates.description: Present when the door's rates are off, lamp-control's default (`--rates default` turns them on): every rate lifted but `refused` and `phrases`, whose windows are then the only ones told.

quiet_hours.description: This lamp's quiet hours (lamp-control's --quiet-hours or LAMP_CONTROL_QUIET; "off" unless set): when set, `say` and `sound` are refused inside them, local times from `from` up to `to`, across midnight when `to` comes first; or "off".

lease_max_ms.description: The longest one lease take or renewal asks for (600000); renewed in time, a lease has no ceiling. `hold_max_ms` stays a light's longest `for_ms` (30000).

say_max_bytes.description: The longest say's text in UTF-8 bytes (900), the voice's own cap.

sounds.description: A computer's own clips (sound.upload): the clip's rate and longest, its largest file, how it is sent, and each computer's store.

notes.description: A computer's own notes (notes.set): a key's and a value's largest, how many keys and bytes each computer keeps, and the rates of writes (set, delete) and reads (get, list).

motion_done.description: Present when a `gesture`, `move` or feeling's move ends with a `done` once the body says what became of it (#4209): `finished` at its end, `dropped` (never began: the person using the lamp, a move it can't play, nothing begun within 10 s) or `cut_short` (ended as it played: replaced by a newer motion, or for the person), each with the body's `why`. Without it, a lamp-control from before reads no word from the body, and an SDK's wait for them ends at the answer.

ring.description: The ring as light's pixels see it.

pixels.description: How many pixels, from pixel 0 around the ring.

presence.description: How many people, how near, whether one faces the lamp. Never who.

quiet_hours.description: Planned: not produced yet. With quiet hours set (off by default), the door refuses say and sound in them, or while the lamp's local time isn't known, with the error `quiet_hours` (control.md, quiet hours); this state key is a later piece.

lease.description: Who holds a lease now, by client name, if anyone.

at.description: When it happened, in UTC (`…Z`), on the events about the room. welcome, lease and done may not carry it.

then.description: The lamp's first frame on every connection: the nonce pair's proof and hello's signature cover.

nonce.description: 32 random bytes, base64, new for each connection.

language.description: The owner's language (en, vi, ja, zh or ko), from the lamp's setup, so a program's own lines can follow it; en when the owner has not chosen one. Lamps from before this say none: read it as en.

score.description: How sure the lamp's listener was that it heard its name, to a hundredth. A sound like the name can reach the lamp's own bar, so a program that acts on its own may want a higher one.

then.description: A hand in view (humans/hands/tracked, on the lamp): told when it is first seen, moves or grows by 0.05 of the picture, opens or closes, at most four times a second; and once when gone, after 1 s with no hand. Where it is in the picture, never the picture, its keypoints or whose hand.

x.description: The palm's centre, as a share of the picture's width from its left edge.

y.description: The palm's centre, as a share of the picture's height from its top edge.

size.description: The palm's width as a share of the picture's width.

open.description: An open hand; false for a closed one.

confidence.description: How sure the tracker is that it is a hand, from 0.5: below that it isn't one.

joints.description: Each joint the body read, named as the joints op names them.

lamp.description: The lamp's own state beside the joints: the light it shows now, whether it talks, whether it is private.

yaw.description: A look's done: the yaw the head reached, degrees, right positive.

pitch.description: A look's done: the pitch the head reached, degrees, up positive.

clamped.description: A look's done: the body held it inside its reach or pitch window, so yaw and pitch are not what was asked.

then.description: The air sensor's reading (air/state, the air grant): the first one, then one where a value moved by its step (particles 5 µg/m³, carbon dioxide 50 ppm, humidity 3, temperature 0.5 °C), came or went, or feel changed; at most once every 5 s, the newest held back until then.

pm1_0.description: Particles under 1 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm2_5.description: Particles under 2.5 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm4_0.description: Particles under 4 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm10.description: Particles under 10 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

humidity.description: Relative humidity at the sensor, percent, to a tenth.

temperature.description: Degrees Celsius at the sensor, to a tenth: inside the lamp's base, warmed by the lamp, so not the room's.

feel.description: How the air would feel, from the carbon dioxide: fresh under 800 ppm, fine to 1,200, stuffy to 2,000, very_stuffy past it, unknown without a reading.

level.description: 0 to 100 of what the lamp allows.

text.description: What the lamp said out loud, as written (for a reply, what the model wrote; see cut).

by.description: Who had it said: the lamp itself, or a computer's own say (back to that computer alone).

source.description: A reply of the lamp's model, a computer's word-for-word say, or one of the lamp's fixed phrases.

cut.description: Present only when the line was cut short (talked over, stopped): text may not have been said in full.

then.description: One new picture of a camera.stream.

fps_now.description: The eyes' rate of new frames over the last 2 s; null before two were seen.

then.description: The camera.stream ended by itself: the lamp turned private, or the camera stayed closed.
One block of a microphone.stream, the header of its binary WebSocket message (the sound itself follows the header, never in JSON).

sequence.description: The block's count since the ears started; a step of more than one is sound that was lost.

lost.description: Blocks lost since the last one this stream sent: gaps in sequence, and blocks the connection had no room for.

bytes.description: The sound's size in bytes: 640 for a 20 ms block.

then.description: The microphone.stream ended by itself: the lamp turned private, someone else came into view (more than one person), or no sound came for 2 s (the lamp's microphone isn't shared here).

air.description: The air sensor's newest reading (air/state, every 5 s). A value the sensor doesn't know yet is left out.

pm1_0.description: Particles under 1 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm2_5.description: Particles under 2.5 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm4_0.description: Particles under 4 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

pm10.description: Particles under 10 µm, µg/m³, to a tenth.

humidity.description: Relative humidity at the sensor, percent, to a tenth.

temperature.description: Degrees Celsius at the sensor, to a tenth: inside the lamp's base, warmed by the lamp, so not the room's.

feel.description: How the air would feel, from the carbon dioxide: fresh under 800 ppm, fine to 1,200, stuffy to 2,000, very_stuffy past it, unknown without a reading.

device.description: The lamp's own computer (board/state, every 5 s).

cpu_load.description: The last minute's load over the processors: 1 is every processor busy.

memory_used.description: The share of memory in use.

disk_free.description: The share of the system disk free.

temperature_c.description: Each temperature the board reports, by its sensor's name, in degrees Celsius.

body.description: get's body (the body grant): what the body may do and where each joint is, from body/limits and body/joint_states, with known: true; or known: false and why, while the body has said no limits in the last 15 s. Nothing here can be raised.

known.description: Whether the body has said its limits in the last 15 s; false, and then only why.

joints.description: By the names joints takes; a joint the body didn't name is left out.

stands.description: Whether this lamp may stand; with false, the arm has no poses.

speed_deg_s.description: The head's and base's speed cap, degrees a second.

acceleration_deg_s2.description: The head's and base's acceleration cap, degrees a second squared.

load_limit.description: The force cap as a share; null where each servo keeps its own.

heat_stop_c.description: Where a joint stops for heat, degrees Celsius.

get_body_joint.description: One joint of get's body: where it is and its bounds, in counts (4,096 a turn) and in degrees from its home (body_info::from_home). A number is null when not known.

counts.description: Where it is now, of 4,096 a turn; null with no position in the last 15 s.

deg.description: Degrees from its home, to a tenth; null with no position in the last 15 s.

min_deg.description: Its lowest bound in degrees from home. The head's and base's are a folded lamp's: don't clamp a target to them.

max_deg.description: Its highest bound in degrees from home. The head's and base's are a folded lamp's: don't clamp a target to them.

home_counts.description: Its home, counts: the found home for the head and base, the folded pose for the arm.

folded_counts.description: The arm's folded pose, counts; null for the head and base.

stand_counts.description: The arm's stand pose, counts; null for the head and base.

volume.description: The speaker's volume, the person's own (the same the voice and the app set, through lamp-actions): exactly one of a level, a step or a mute. Needs the speak grant; no rate. The reply is the level it left, {level, muted}.

to.description: A level, 0 to 100 of what the lamp allows; 0 is muted.

step.description: The voice's own step, within the lamp's floor and ceiling.

mute.description: true mutes; false brings it back to where it was.

camera.snapshot.description: The camera's newest picture, once, as the eyes keep it (a JPEG about 320 across). Needs the camera grant. Refused while the lamp is private (private) or with the camera closed (refused: the camera is closed).

camera.stream.description: The camera's pictures as camera.frame events, each new frame once as it comes, at most fps a second (1 to 30, 2 if not given; today the eyes give about 1 to 2 new frames a second), until on is false, stop, the connection closes, or a camera.ended event (the lamp turned private, or the camera closed for 10 s). The answer's fps_now is the rate new frames came at lately, null before any was measured. Needs the camera grant; refused while the lamp is private. Where the eyes serve every frame (the answer's fast: true), each comes as a binary WebSocket message: the header's length (4 bytes, big-endian), the header (JSON: ev camera.frame, bytes, width, height, fps_now), then the JPEG as the camera made it, at most 512 KiB.

size.description: The fast stream's size, where the eyes serve every frame: the camera's own 25 fps MJPEG modes. 640x480 if not given.

body_joint.description: One joint in a body.state: where it is, from the body's own read.

deg.description: Where it is, in degrees from its home, to a tenth, as get('body') counts them: from the found home for the head and base and the folded pose for the arm; yaw, shoulder, elbow and roll positive with more counts, pitch positive looking up. null until the body has said its limits.

counts.description: Where it is, in the servo's own encoder counts: 4,096 a turn, 2,048 its middle.

goal_deg.description: Where it was last asked to be, in the same degrees as deg.

load.description: How hard it works: the share of its servo's full strength, without a direction.

moving.description: Turning at 5 degrees a second or more.

temp_c.description: Its servo's temperature, from the body's once-a-second report; absent until the first.

microphone.stream.description: The microphone's sound, each 20 ms block the ears share on mic1/audio (mono, 16 kHz, S16LE), as a binary WebSocket message: the header's length (4 bytes, big-endian), the header (JSON: ev microphone.audio, sequence, lost, sample_rate, channels, format, bytes), then the samples, 640 bytes. Until on is false, stop, the connection closes, or a microphone.ended event (the lamp turned private, someone else came into view, or no block came for 2 s: the ears share their sound only with LAMP_BUS_AUDIO=on). On again while one runs replaces it. Needs the microphone grant, the lamp's own network and the owner's switch (lamp-control --microphone on, LAMP_CONTROL_MICROPHONE=on; off unless given: refused, the microphone stream is off on this lamp). Refused while the lamp is private, while more than one person is in view (refused: someone else is here; the door can't tell the owner from anyone else), and where the ring can't show its mark; either of the first two also ends a running stream with microphone.ended.

service_grant.description: A linked service's grant, a skill run's alone (on the control socket, from the owner's yes; never a paired computer's): <code>-read reads it, <code>-write prepares a write the person's spoken yes sends. The codes are lamp-services' (gmail covers gmail-app, figma covers figma-api).

service_code.description: A linked service's code, as lamp-services' catalog has it.

service.read.description: A skill's run only (the control socket, LAMP_SKILL_TASKS=on): one read of a linked service through lamp-services' service_read, args as that function takes them, without service. Needs the <service>-read grant. The reply's result is lamp-services' answer; its refusal comes as refused, with off while the switch is off.

args.description: service_read's own arguments (what, query, id, count, ...), never service. Personal: never logged.

service.write.description: A skill's run only (the control socket, LAMP_SKILL_TASKS=on): one write to a linked service, only prepared by lamp-services' service_write, read back and held for the person's spoken yes, which sends it; never sent by the run. Needs the <service>-write grant. The reply's result is the read_back, sent false and held true, with no send_id.
